sara: quick heads-up — ran Gorilla-v1 (768d) through a 5-fold stratified kfold on the legal-docs holdout. saw a weird collapse in R@10 on fold 3 when using int8 quant. sharing raw run + notes.

liam: ugh. numbers?

sara: pasted results below (cols: R@1,R@5,R@10, silhouette)
```
fold1: 0.45, 0.71, 0.83, 0.22
fold2: 0.46, 0.69, 0.82, 0.21
fold3: 0.12, 0.37, 0.59, 0.05  <-- big drop
fold4: 0.44, 0.70, 0.84, 0.24
fold5: 0.47, 0.72, 0.85, 0.23
```

jin: that’s nasty. was fold3 skewed (short queries / few labels)?

sara: fold3 has higher fraction of short legal-sections (avg query tokens 6.1 vs 12.4 overall). also more near-duplicates.

natalie: what index + recall impl? cosine? annoy/hnsw?

sara: HNSW (ef_search=128, M=32), cosine. recall computed with top-k cosine nearest. eval run command:
```
python tools/eval_kfold.py --model gorilla-v1 --quant int8 --folds 5 --k 10 --metric recall --index hnsw --ef 128 --seed 42
```

liam: have you repro'd float32 for same fold?

sara: yes — float32 baseline: fold3 R@10 = 0.83 (consistent with other folds). so issue only with quantized path.

jin: possible causes: quantization noise interacting with very short queries (small dot products -> lower SNR), or a preprocessing mismatch between train/serve (padding/tokenization). did you try per-channel vs per-tensor quant?

sara: int8 was per-tensor symmetric (our default ONNX export). per-channel not tested yet.

natalie: can you dump a few query vs positive neighbor pairs for fold3 where int8 fails? would like to inspect embedding deltas + norms.

sara: yes — attached small sample below (showing float vs int8 cosine):
```
q1: float_cos( p1 )=0.87  int8_cos=0.21
q1: float_cos( p2 )=0.84  int8_cos=0.19
q2: float_cos( p1 )=0.65  int8_cos=0.60  # stable
q3: float_cos( p1 )=0.79  int8_cos=0.12
```

jin: wild — some embeddings are collapsing (norms near zero?) check L2 norm distribution.

sara: l2 norms: float (mean=1.02, std=0.12), int8 (mean=0.11, std=0.09) on fold3 queries. looks like scaling bug in quantization path.

eval-bot: auto-repro job completed (run id: eq-4100009876-01). Per-channel int8 build yields fold3 R@10=0.81.

liam: that narrows it — per-tensor was the culprit. do we know which op/export stage used per-tensor?

sara: ONNX export + `quantize_dynamic` with default params led to per-tensor scales.

natalie: actionables: 1) re-run int8 with per-channel quant (eval-bot did quick run) 2) add a short-query stratified check to our kfold harness (flag: --stratify-query-len) 3) add embedding-norm histogram to nightly smoke.

jin: + add a CI check: if mean(int8_norm)/mean(float_norm) < 0.6 for any fold -> fail and attach top-10 worst queries.

ops-bot: flagged a related dedicated deployment canary (gorilla-v1-int8) to pause rollout until post-quant sanity checks pass. @sara please confirm when fixed so we can unpause. :white_check_mark:

sara: will do. immediate next steps: (A) re-export ONNX with per-channel quant and re-run full 5-fold stratified kfold incl stratify-by-query-len, (B) add hist/norm check to eval output, (C) generate UMAP + silhouette for fold3 to visualize micro-clusters.

liam: want help with UMAP plotting — I can take (C). jin + sara do (A/B) and ping when done.

natalie: nice catch, sara. once we have per-channel numbers we can decide whether to promote int8 build to staging.

sara: noted. updating the ticket: https://redwood-internal/boards/EV-1782 

liam: thanks — keep the thread updated. :coffee:

eval-bot: attached quick diff: per-tensor int8 mean_R@10 = 0.67, per-channel int8 mean_R@10 = 0.82, float32 mean_R@10 = 0.84. (detailed CSV in artifact store)

sara: perfect — closing the loop here once per-channel runs finish. thanks everyone.
